identity.name: Lim dynasty of Mari
alt_names: Second kingdom of Mari under the Lim dynasty

land.text: the Suhum region, which "became a Babylonian province" after 1761

successors.note: Terqa "became the capital of the rump Kingdom of Hana" (Mari page); the Hana kings are not mapped (no dossier).

capitals.name: Mari (Tell Hariri)
capitals.note: The Lim dynasty's seat from c. 1830; Shamshi-Adad I held Mari c. 1796-1776 (Yasmah-Adad on the throne). Zimri-Lim was crowned in Terqa.

rulers.name: Yaggid-Lim
rulers.note: The page doubts he controlled Mari; end year derived from Yahdun-Lim "firmly in control" c. 1820.

rulers.name: Sumu-Yamam
rulers.note: Assassinated two years after taking the throne.

rulers.name: Zimri-Lim
rulers.note: The Zimri-Lim page: reign c. 1775-1760 (high chronology).

correction.text: the Euphrates from Mari through Terqa to Tuttul: "Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1830..-1797: no Cliopatria shape. Yahdun-Lim's "titles were king of Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana"; the Mari page lists the provincial seats Terqa, Saggarâtum, Qaṭṭunān and Tuttul. Drawn as circles along the Euphrates from Mari to Tuttul (my reading; the pages give no frontier). The page says nothing of Suhum, the Balikh or the Habur under Yahdun-Lim.

correction.text: the Euphrates from Mari to Tuttul and the Suhum region

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1776..-1771: Zimri-Lim "advanced along the Euphrates, taking Tuttul and then Terqa" and "entered Mari and was crowned in Terqa" after Shamshi-Adad I died. Suhum was Mari's by fall 1772, when Eshnunna invaded it, and "became a Babylonian province" in 1761 (Mari page). No keyframe for -1796..-1777: Shamshi-Adad I held Mari and the dynasty was in exile.

correction.text: the Euphrates valley from Tuttul to Suhum and the Upper Khabur region

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1771..-1761: Zimri-Lim "defeated Qarni-Lim of Andarig, securing the Mariote control over the region in c. 1771 BC" and "expanded into the Upper Khabur region (Idamaraz)"; "Its territory included the Upper Khabur region and the Euphrates valley". The Upper Khabur is a circle at 41.5 E 36.5 N (my reading; Andarig is unlocated on the pages).

ledger.note: c. 1830 BC: Mari becomes the seat of the Lim dynasty. "Mari became the seat of the Amorite Lim dynasty under king Yaggid-Lim" c. 1830 BC; the page notes it is not certain he controlled Mari, and that "in c. 1820 BC Yahdun-Lim was firmly in control as king of Mari". The land is Mari's district (my reading).

region.text: Terqa, the Euphrates up river and Tuttul, the Yaminite centre

ledger.note: c. 1810 BC (bridged to mid-reign): Yahdun-Lim holds Tuttul and expands up the Euphrates. His titles were "king of Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana"; "He defeated the Yaminite rebels centered at Tuttul" (Mari page); the pages give no year (reign c. 1820-1797) and the Mediterranean campaign he "claimed" is undated and not territory.

region.text: Mari and the Lim kingdom along the Euphrates

ledger.note: c. 1796 BC: Shamshi-Adad I takes Mari. Yahdun-Lim "was assassinated in c. 1798 BC by his possible son Sumu-Yamam" (also: killed in battle with Shamshi-Adad c. 1796); Sumu-Yamam "was assassinated two years after taking the throne, and Shamshi-Adad then annexed Mari", appointing Yasmah-Adad; the rest of the Lim family fled to Yamhad. The assyria dossier books only Mari for Shamshi-Adad I; the kingdom's other seats are not on the page and are shown as lost here.

c. 1776 BC: Zimri-Lim returns to Mari. The Mari page: "a short time after his enthronement in c. 1776 BC"; Zimri-Lim's page: Samsi-Addu died in 1775, Yasmah-Addu disappeared from the record and Zimri-Lim "entered Mari and was crowned in Terqa". Shamshi-Adad I's page: "Yasmah-Adad was soon expelled from Mari by Zimri-Lim". Mirrors the assyria loss.

region.text: Terqa, the middle Euphrates and Tuttul

ledger.counterpart: Yaminite and Bensimalite chiefs (Tuttul, Terqa, Mari)
ledger.note: c. 1775 BC: Zimri-Lim takes Tuttul and Terqa. "Zimri-Lim advanced along the Euphrates, taking Tuttul and then Terqa." The page adds that Bannum, a Bensimalite warlord, seized Mari, and that Ishme-Dagan "kept Ekallatum but could not intervene in Mari".

region.text: Suhum on the middle Euphrates between Mari and Hit

ledger.note: c. 1775 BC (bridged): the Suhum region. The pages say nothing of how Mari got Suhum; the Zimri-Lim page has Eshnunna invading it in fall 1772, and the Mari page has it a Babylonian province after 1761. Held by 1772, so shown from the restoration. Page silent on the date and the previous holder.
Fall 1772 BC: Eshnunna invades Suhum. "The Mari-Eshnunna conflict erupted in the fall of 1772, when Eshnunna invaded Suhum."

region.text: the Upper Khabur region around Andarig

ledger.note: c. 1771 BC: the Upper Khabur. Zimri-Lim "defeated Qarni-Lim of Andarig, securing the Mariote control over the region in c. 1771 BC", and "expanded into the Upper Khabur region (Idamaraz)". The Zimri-Lim page has Eshnunna defeated at Andarig (no year).
1770 BC: peace. "Peace: it was concluded in 1770. Zimri-Lim recognized Ibal-pi-El as his father, and regained the lost territories."

region.text: the whole kingdom of Mari, conquered by Babylon

ledger.note: c. 1761 BC: Hammurabi ends the Lim dynasty. "Babylon invaded in c. 1761 BC under the rule of Hammurabi and defeated Zimri-Lin, ending the Lim dynasty." Terqa became the capital of the rump Kingdom of Hana and the Suhum region a Babylonian province; the Zimri-Lim page: Babylon captured Mari "apparently in the spring of 1761", the circumstances unknown (the Babylonia page allows a surrender). Mari rebelled c. 1759 and Hammurabi razed it (after the end of this dossier).

wars.name: Yahdun-Lim against the Yaminites and Shamshi-Adad I
wars.outcome: Yahdun-Lim defeated the Yaminite rebels at Tuttul (backed by Sumu-Epuh of Yamhad) and avoided open war with Yamhad; "later lost a war to Shamshi-Adad" and died c. 1798/1796; Sumu-Yamam was killed two years on.
wars.note: The page is itself inconsistent: assassinated c. 1798 by Sumu-Yamam, or killed in battle with Shamshi-Adad c. 1796 (Hamblin).

wars.name: Shamshi-Adad I's annexation of Mari
wars.outcome: Shamshi-Adad I put Yasmah-Adad on the throne of Mari c. 1796; Zimri-Lim expelled him after the king's death c. 1776.

wars.name: Zimri-Lim's restoration along the Euphrates

zones.text: the Euphrates from Mari to Tuttul

wars.outcome: Zimri-Lim took Tuttul and then Terqa and entered Mari; Bannum, a Bensimalite warlord, held Mari for a time.

wars.name: Mari-Eshnunna war
wars.outcome: Eshnunna invaded Suhum in fall 1772; its forces were defeated at Andarig; peace in 1770 with the lost territories regained.

wars.name: Elamite war and the coalition with Babylon
wars.outcome: Mari allied with Elam in 1766-1765; Elam "captured it [Eshnunna] in 1765"; Zimri-Lim and Hammurabi then defeated the Elamites at Hiritum in northern Babylonia (undated).
wars.note: The page: "A war with Elam involved both kingdoms in c. 1765 BC", after a dispute over Hit.

wars.name: Hammurabi's conquest of Mari
wars.outcome: Babylon defeated Zimri-Lim c. 1761 and ended the Lim dynasty; the Suhum region became a Babylonian province; Mari rebelled and was razed c. 1759.

certainty.note: The pages give titles and provincial seats, not a frontier.
The Lim dynasty held no land: Mari was Shamshi-Adad I's (assyria dossier) and the family was in exile.
The Upper Khabur and Suhum limits are readings; Andarig is unlocated on the pages.

sources.title: Yahdun-Lim
sources.note: Reign c. 1820-1797; titles king of Mari, Tuttul and Hana; Yaminites at Tuttul; death c. 1797/1796; Shamshi-Adad.

sources.title: Zimri-Lim
sources.note: Reign c. 1775-1760; return from exile; Tuttul and Terqa; Eshnunna from fall 1772; peace 1770; Elam 1765; Hammurabi 1761.

sources.title: Mari, Syria
sources.note: The Amorite Lim dynasty c. 1830-1761: Yaggid-Lim, Yahdun-Lim, Sumu-Yamam, Shamshi-Adad, Zimri-Lim, Andarig 1771, Elam 1765, Hammurabi 1761 and 1759, the four provincial seats.

sources.title: Shamshi-Adad I
sources.note: Mari occupied c. 1796 with Yasmah-Adad on the throne; Zimri-Lim expels him after the king's death c. 1776. Read for assyria.

notes:
SCOPE. State Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names empty). The earlier kingdom of Mari (-2900..-2290) is the existing mari dossier (me-01 or earlier); the Shakkanakku interval between is on no opened page and has no dossier here, so predecessors is empty. Years: -1830 and -1761 from the Mari page; the brief's suggested span.
PAGES. Three own pages (Mari Syria, Yahdun-Lim, Zimri-Lim) plus Shamshi-Adad I, shared with the assyria dossier.
GAP -1796..-1777. Shamshi-Adad I held Mari (assyria gain -1796, loss -1776); the Lim family was in exile (Yamhad or Aleppo). No keyframe covers those years and the ledger records the loss. Both pages for the exile: Yahdun-Lim page "fled to Aleppo", Zimri-Lim page "within the kingdom of Yamhad, or at least under its protection ... fifteen years in exile".
REGIONS. All circles are readings of names: the pages give no coordinates or frontiers. Gazetteer names missing: Mari (Tell Hariri), Terqa, Tuttul, Saggaratum, Qattunan, Suhum, Andarig, Idamaraz, Hit region. The -1796 loss shows the whole chain as lost while the assyria dossier books only the Mari circle (the page speaks of Mari alone).
DISAGREEMENTS. Yahdun-Lim death c. 1798 (assassinated by Sumu-Yamam) vs c. 1796 (killed by Shamshi-Adad, Hamblin); Old Assyrian period page: victory over Yahdun-Lim c. 1792. Zimri-Lim's enthronement c. 1776 (Mari page) vs 1775 (his page; reign "c. 1775-1760 high chronology", "c. 1767-1752 middle chronology"). Zimri-Lim page: Bannum seized Mari and Yasmah-Addu disappears; Mari page: a Sim'alite leader overthrew him; the Shamshi-Adad I page: Zimri-Lim expelled him.
NOT IN LEDGER. Zimri-Lim's vassal kings in the Khabur (1767, names not on the page); Yamhad relations (marriage to Shibtu, daughter of Yarim-Lim I; the Yamhad dossier belongs to another group); Ishme-Dagan regained Ekallatum after the Elamite war; the Mari-Hammurabi alliance and the Hit dispute.
MIRRORS. assyria (gain -1796, loss -1776); eshnunna (contest -1772..-1770); babylonia (gain -1761). The Kingdom of Hana (Terqa after 1761) needs a dossier.
